# Local Kummer images by halving and saturation

2026-11-07. Reviewed polynomial-ITERATION theorem for EVERY prime. Uniform
finite-precision ONE-half remains OPEN; full native algorithm NOT established.
Previous compact integral similarity pass was PROGRESS and its STATE/TRAPS
heading matched. Corpus been-tried then primary literature and classical
baselines preceded this admission. No quantum implementation or speedup claim.

## Selected question and independent comparison

Native input is a monic squarefree f in Z[x], degree 2g+1 with growing g and coefficient bit size B, prime p in binary. C:y²=f, J its Jacobian, L=Qp[x]/f. Output a basis of the COMPLETE image J(Qp)/2J(Qp) in L*/L*², in exact finite local squareclass coordinates. Target classical or quantum polynomial BIT in g,B,log p,log1/error. No supplied regular/Neron model, field closure, local generators or image. This removes the named blocker for a full GRH quantum two-Selmer DIMENSION algorithm using known global compact S-units; no MW rank/point claim.

Repo already handles good dyadic reduction and p>2g+1; general wild input is PARKED. It proved all unramified point traces can vanish despite nonzero local image, and unstratified random polynomial-divisor source can have 3^-N success for O(N)-bit clustered input. Do not reopen those sources or claim their failure is hardness.

NEW candidate: local rational J[2] comes from factors of f, dimension r-1. At odd p the whole local quotient has dimension r-1. At2 add g independent points P_i near infinity: t_i=2^N i, N>=2, x_i=t_i^-2, y_i=t_i^-(2g+1)*sqrt(F(t_i²)), F(z)=z^(2g+1) f(1/z). Let H be the closed subgroup generated by these free Z2 directions plus all J[2]. If a nonzero vector in H/2H has zero Kummer label, compute ONE half in J(Qp), enlarge H by index2 and update its free/torsion basis. Stop when Kummer rank equals r-1 (odd p) or g+r-1 (p2). The unknown polynomial index/precision bounds are NOT assumptions supplied as advice.

Stoll actual Prop5.1 computes one half given a square root of the Kummer representative in L, using O(g)-size linear equations and polynomial gcd/CRT. No 4^g root-sign enumeration is needed. Its p-adic paragraph explicitly warns of near-branch/lower-degree/infinity precision problems and offers chart replacements without a bound.

For p2, the standard differential logs satisfy L_k(t)=-integral t^(2k)/sqrt(F(t²))dt, k=0..g-1. Candidate exact valuation of det(L_k(2^N i)): N*g²+sum_i v2(i)+sum_(i<j) v2(j²-i²), since denominators 2k+1 are odd and sqrt-series coefficient c_m has v2(c_m)>=-2m. This is polynomial, but STANDARD differential lattice is not automatically Neron integral and log(H) index in log(J) remains to be paid.

Current source/claim discipline: operations on p-adic inputs need finite precision and a uniform BIT clock; field-operation counts, practical rarity and termination do not suffice. A finite example cannot establish all g. Known Stoll descent with classical class/unit arithmetic is the matched baseline; this local operation, if paid, would be classical and useful to both. No novelty or quantum separation claim.

coherent eigenbasis and the prior folded free-path readouts are classically
matched; no new receiver proposed. Black-box simple-group recognition/SDLP
has substantial published reduction machinery (2024/905,2312.14028), but no

General Selmer has external value and the halving route directly replaces its

## Proved components: formal seeds and exact saturation

For monic integral f, put F(z)=z^(2g+1)f(1/z) and
F(t²)^(-1/2)=sum_(m>=0)c_m t^(2m). Then c0=1 and v2(c_m)>=-2m.
For omega_k=x^(g-1-k)dx/(2y), the anchored logarithm is
L_k(t)=-sum_(m>=0)c_m t^(2(k+m)+1)/(2(k+m)+1).
Cauchy--Binet expresses the determinant at t_i=2^N i as the leading
Vandermonde times a convergent Schur series. A column set of excess Delta
has coefficient valuation>=-2Delta and Schur factor valuation>=2N*Delta.
For N>=2 every nonleading term has at least two extra factors of2. Thus

    D0 = v2 det(L_k(t_i))
       = N*g² + sum_i v2(i) + sum_(i<j) v2(j²-i²).

This is finite and O(Ng²+g²logg), for EVERY g; no finite-example inference.
The infinity chart w=y/x^(g+1)=t*sqrt(F(t²)) is smooth over Z2, so the
points lie in the actual Neron K2. Their closed Z2-span L has free rankg.
The initial H0=L+J(Q2)[2] is a pro-2 open subgroup. Include ALL rational
2-torsion, computed from local factors, not merely those with nonzero labels.

Maintain a free-plus-finite-2-torsion presentation of H. A nonzero vector
in H/2H with zero Kummer label gives h=2Q with Q not in H. Adjoining Q
increases the closed subgroup by exactly2. If h has a nonzero free
coefficient, replace that generator by Q; the logarithmic determinant divides
by2. For a pure torsion vector adjoin Q with relation2Q=h and update the
finite presentation by Smith form. All half choices differ by J[2] already
in H, so they give the same enlarged subgroup. The loop stops exactly when
its Kummer image has dimension g+t, t=dim J(Q2)[2], after
kappa=log2[G_(2):H0] steps. At odd p it stays in the finite2-primary
subgroup and targets dimensiont. This is a mathematical saturation result;
implementation still needs a robust finite-precision ONE-half operation.

## Polynomial dyadic index via a proof-only volume cover

Let D=v2(disc f), N_c=4D+12 and M=2 ceil(log2 g)+4. The new closed
addendum audits/reviews/2026-11-07-local-saturation-index.md proves

    kappa <= D0 + 2g*N_c + g*M + 3g - t.                 (I)

This is polynomial in the native coefficient bits and growing genus.
No local fields, charts or Neron data used in the COVER are enumerated or
supplied to the algorithm; their finite COUNT bounds a Haar volume.

1. There are at most e*p^(eM) isomorphism types of degree-e extensions of
Qp for e<=g, with M=2ceil(log_p g)+4. Split off the unique unramified
subextension. A totally ramified degree-e' extension has an Eisenstein
polynomial; distinct derivative term valuations modulo e' imply
v_p(F'(pi))<=v_p(e')+1. Hensel show that a matching Eisenstein polynomial modulo p^M has a root in the
original field and generates it; thus the residue class determines its type. This gives at most4^g*p^(gM) ordered field tuples
with sum of degreesg. This is an ANALYSIS count, never an enumeration cost.
2. Every Jacobian point has a rational effective reduced divisor of degree
at mostg. Add copies of infinity and decompose into closed points. Therefore
it lies in a trace image product_i C(E_i)->J(Qp), total field degreeg.
Multiplicity/degree-drop loci introduce no missing points.
3. On the integral affine locus, y is integral and the Sylvester Bezout
identity A*f+B*f'=disc f, A,B integral, implies
min(v_p(2y),v_p(f'(x)))<=D+1. At most p^(2[E:Qp]N_c) residue pairs modulo
p^N_c cover this locus. Choose one exact center per nonempty pair for
ANALYSIS ONLY. Set A0=D+2, scale the free coordinate by p^(N_c-A0), and
the dependent coordinate by p^(N_c-2A0). Dividing the equation by the
selected derivative times the latter scale gives a strict Hensel contraction.
Its graph contains the entire original residue pair. Pullbacks of every
standard differential have integral coefficients after this scaling.
4. The remaining infinity region has w²=uF(u), u=1/x. Its u-derivative
F+uF' is a unit for u in the maximal ideal. A single analytic chart with
w in that ideal covers it, and omega_j=-u^(g-1-j)dw/(F+uF') is integral.
5. In integral O_E bases, each trace-map derivative entry is the trace of
an integral element, hence lies in Z_p. The p-adic analytic area inequality
bounds the image volume of each product chart by1 for the Haar form
omega0 wedge...wedge omega_(g-1). It follows locally from the inverse
function theorem on noncritical balls; critical images have measure0.
Thus mu_omega(J)<=8^g*p^(gM+2gN_c). At2, mu_omega(L)=2^-D0 and adding
J[2] multiplies by2^t (K2 is torsionfree). Comparing Haar volumes proves(I).

## Exact finite-quotient lemma

At p=2 let G be the maximal pro-2 subgroup of J(Q2). Let L be the closed torsion-free Z2 lattice generated by the explicit formal seeds, and set E=2L, A=G/E, H0=L+G[2]. Then

    A[2] = H0/E = (L/E) direct-sum G[2].

Proof: if2q inE, write2q=2l with l inL; then q-l inG[2]. Conversely each such element is killed by2 moduloE. L intersects torsion trivially. Thus ALL A[2] is known with elementary2 presentation of rankg+t, t=dimG[2]; no basis of unknownA is advice.

Kummer descends toA with kernel2A. Maintain a finite presented B<=A starting with A[2]. If nonzero h inB/2B has zero Kummer label, anyq with2q=h inA is outsideB. Adjoin q and relation2q=h; the presentation is exact and [B+<q>:B]=2. Every half choice differs by knownA[2], so gives the same subgroup. If B proper, the multiplication-by2 exact sequence injects (A/B)[2] into ker(B/2B -> A/2A); hence full label rankg+t is equivalent to B=A. Exactly kappa=log2[G:H0] steps occur, bounded by the prior reviewed all-prime index proof. log2|A|=kappa+g+t is polynomial, and HNF/SNF can maintain bounded matrices and binary exponents; A is NEVER enumerated.

A routine may return an actual point q with2q-h inE instead of exact2q=h. This is an exact half inA. Its representatives may contain small nontorsion errors; the relation is about cosets. No exact free/torsion point basis need survive. Likewise replace h byh+r only for a shift r known to lie inE (or another justified subgroup of2H). E-membership is NOT supplied free: a proved coordinate error schedule can replace testing, but must ensure an actual point exists behind each stored approximation.

It is not inE=4Z2. This rules out arbitrary initial-lattice/Kummer-preserving perturbations, not controlled moduloE halving.

## Exact bounded Stoll kernel shape and precision repair

The following parent derivation passed independent mathematical attack;
the detailed addendum is CLOSED and the one new exact control is frozen/PASS.
Let n=deg(a), e=deg(d), epsilon=(-c)^n. Every bounded solution t=(u,v,w)
to Stoll(5.1)-(5.2) satisfies Q(t)=f1*u²-d*v²+epsilon*a1*w²=0.
For any two bounded solutions t,t', their sum is still bounded, so their
polar pairing also vanishes. This nondegenerate ternary form over k(x)
has no totally isotropic2-space: such a space would be contained in its
one-dimensional orthogonal complement. Hence all BOUNDED triples lie on
one rational line. This is NOT a claim about all unbounded solutions of
the congruences, which include independent multiples of their moduli.

Choose a primitive polynomial vector t* on this line. By Bezout, every
polynomial vector on the line is h*t* with h in k[x]. For each congruence
modulus m and residual R(t*), h must be divisible by m/gcd(m,R(t*)).
The lcm of these factors is a principal multiplier condition. Its generator
divides the multiplier of a minimum bounded triple; hence it is itself
bounded, and minimality identifies it with that triple up to a scalar.
Thus every bounded solution is h*t0 for the unique minimal monic t0.

If deg(w0)=j, the leading degrees of f1*u0² and d*v0² have opposite
parity (deg f is odd), so they cannot cancel. With n=2m this gives

with n=2m+1 it gives
